english.title: Do an act which harmed a witness / juror

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing or believing that **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) or another had

(A)_[assisted in the investigation of an offence,]_
(B)_[given evidence in proceedings for an offence,]_
(C)_[given particular evidence in proceedings for an offence,]_
(D)_[acted as a juror in proceedings for an offence,]_
(E)_[concurred in a particular verdict in proceedings for an offence,]_

and because of what you knew or believed did an act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..),

(F)_[which harmed, and was intended to harm, **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(G)_[which would have harmed, and was intended to harm, **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 51(2) and (6) of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowing / believing a person / another
had assisted in investigation /
given evidence in proceedings /
given particular evidence in proceedings /
acted as juror /
concurred in a particular verdict
and because of that knowledge / belief
did an act which

a person

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The motive required for the commission of the offence need not be the only or the predominating motive with which the act is done.
(ii) The act may be done to a third party with intent to harm the person referred to in the **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) field.
(iii) The harm done or threatened may be financial as well as physical (whether to the person or property).
(iv) See H2234 for the alternative offence of intimidating a witness/juror.
(v) See offence wording: H1809.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
